summary: Umatilla NF ridge emergency cabin dated 1935 (1933 per Willhite); moved 1950 and 2003 to private land in Whitman County. Firetower lists it gone.

facts.design: L-5 cabin (firelookout.com); called an emergency lookout house by Willhite Web
facts.status_note: Moved off the ridge in 1950 and again in 2003; per Willhite Web it stands in good condition on private property in Whitman County. Former Fire Lookout Sites lists it as gone.

access.note: Cabin is on private property in Whitman County; a 2021 visit was made with special permission. The original ridge is National Forest land reached by forest roads from Pomeroy.

visit.trail_note: Willhite Web: from Pomeroy take 15th Street south, then forest roads to Round Prairie; 500 to 1000 feet of easy walking to the old site. No standing structure is reported there.

events.note: Willhite Web says a 1933 CCC camp built the emergency lookout house. Other sources give 1935.
Dated 1935 by Former Fire Lookout Sites, firelookout.com and Rex's Fire Lookout Page; the Former Fire Lookout Sites panoramas are dated August 7, 1935.
Used for emergencies in the 1940s; no exact start year given.
Moved off the ridge to a farm 4.5 miles northeast (firelookout.com) or 5 miles northeast (Willhite Web). Willhite says possibly moved by Steve Black.

Farm sold to Washington Department of Fish & Wildlife and Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation. Schlee family moved the cabin to family property on another ranch in Whitman County (Willhite Web). firelookout.com says a private farm in Whitman County.

corrections.why: The cabin was moved off the ridge in 1950 and again in 2003. Willhite Web reports it in good condition on private land in Whitman County, and firelookout.com records the 2003 move to a Whitman County farm. The ridge site itself has no reported standing structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Former Fire Lookout Sites, firelookout.com and Rex's page date the cabin to 1935, and the Former Fire Lookout Sites panoramas are dated August 7, 1935. Willhite Web says a 1933 CCC camp built the emergency house. The story reports both and does not choose.
firelookout.com puts the 1950 farm 4.5 miles northeast of the ridge; Willhite Web says 5 miles.

Former Fire Lookout Sites says the cabin is now gone; Willhite Web's 2021 account shows it standing on private land in Whitman County. The story follows Willhite for the present-day state, since it is the only source with a recent description.

notes_for_editor: Build date conflict: 1933 CCC camp (Willhite) vs 1935 (three sources and the 1935 panoramas). Status is corrected from gone to moved; the 2021 description and photos come from Willhite Web alone. The brief's access 'unknown' is answered as private for the cabin; the ridge is National Forest ground with no reported structure. Relocation distance differs (4.5 vs 5 miles). Rex's page lists only 1935 and Removed, with no other detail. No NHLR or NRHP entry was seen for this site in the pages read.
